newsitem.title: UK: BA says American deal has popular support.
newsitem.headline: BA says American deal has popular support.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Thursday 71 percent of people in a survey thought its proposed alliance with American Airlines was "generally a good idea".
BA said independent market researchers Audience Selection, part of Taylor-Nelson-AGB, polled more than a thousand UK air passengers between September 23 and 30.
It said 62 percent of those surveyed felt an "open skies" agreement between the UK and the U.S. was a good idea, with only 10 percent feeling it was not.
UK competition authorities are currently reviewing BA's proposed alliance with American Airlines, part of AMR Corp, and trade and industry minister Ian Lang is expected to report next week.
The plan has drawn fierce criticism from rival airlines, as well as consumer groups and travel agents, who say the alliance would dominate the transatlantic market into London.
Under the planned link-up, BA aims to coordinate its 244 weekly flights from Britain to 22 U.S. destinations with American's 238 flights from seven U.S. airports to 12 European destinations.
